short_title: EPCR-assisted APC transport across mouse BBB
species_models: Mouse in situ brain arterial perfusion; EPCR-severely-deficient mice and PAR1-knockout mice
molecule_format: ~60 kDa native mouse activated protein C (APC); radiolabeled 125I-APC; recombinant 3K3A/5A APC competitors; protein C zymogen comparator
main_endpoint: In-vivo blood-to-brain uptake of native APC; vascular-space-corrected permeability and capillary-depletion distribution
receptor_specificity: RCR252 (EPCR ligand-site blocker) reduced uptake 85.2%; RCR92 nonblocking control ineffective; severely EPCR-deficient mice ~64% lower uptake; PAR1 blockade or deletion no significant impact
luminal_access: Functional blood-facing EPCR access supported in perfused mouse brain; no direct native human-stroke luminal protein quantification
internalization_trafficking: Transport inferred by perfusion kinetics and genetics; endosomal itinerary not directly imaged in this study
directional_bbb_delivery: Yes for APC tracer: arterial blood-to-brain; substantial capillary-depleted brain localization (>85% of measured brain-associated signal)
intact_cargo_recovery: Whole-brain homogenate TCA-precipitable signal >94% at 10 min and HPLC concordance reported (HPLC plots not shown). Intact APC NOT separately quantified in capillary-depleted fraction; not an engineered short peptide or conjugate
quantitative_results: PS cortex 3.11 +/- 0.30, caudate 3.88 +/- 0.60, hippocampus 4.13 +/- 0.62 uL/min/g vs inulin 0.039/0.035/0.041; Km 1.57 +/- 0.24 nM and Vmax 7.2 +/- 1.0 fmol/min/g; ~78-110x inulin
safety_mechanism: Binding site overlaps endogenous APC/protein C function. Reduced-anticoagulant 3K3A/5A variants retain affinity for transport system, but are engineered APC proteins, not demonstration of safe peptide competition
strengths: Native in vivo BBB, vessel/space markers, capillary depletion, intactness biochemical controls, dose-dependence, genetic and antibody perturbations
limitations: Perfused healthy mice, short 10-minute endpoint; no stroke BBB experiment, human in vivo test, engineered peptide, quantified intact isolated interstitial cargo or functional cargo delivery; some HPLC supporting traces not shown
figures_tables: PDF pp. 4-6: Fig 1A/B and Table 1; Fig 2/Table 2/Fig 3; Fig 4A-C
evidence_grade: Direct native-ligand BBB transport; strong receptor-dependence; not short-peptide shuttle validation

species_models: Primary HUVEC; CHO cells transfected with human EPCR and wild-type CHO controls; mouse peripheral tissue histology and plasma clearance
molecule_format: Full-length human coagulation FVII/FVIIa and protein C/APC proteins; AF488-tagged and 125I-labelled ligands
main_endpoint: Surface localization, receptor-ligand endocytosis, Rab11 recycling; apical-to-basal FVIIa transwell passage
receptor_specificity: CHO-EPCR vs untransfected CHO, JRK1494 blocking antibody; nonblocking antibody controls; caveolar/dynamin inhibitor perturbations; nonspecific controls and BSA leak tracer
luminal_access: Accessible EPCR staining in nonpermeabilized HUVEC and CHO-EPCR; native BBB polarity not assessed
internalization_trafficking: FVIIa/APC binding promotes EPCR co-internalization; caveolin-1 colocalization, dynamin- and cholesterol-sensitive, clathrin depletion insensitive; perinuclear Rab11-positive recycling compartment, substantial return to surface
directional_bbb_delivery: FVIIa apical-to-basal across CHO-EPCR transwell (4x or more than Evans Blue-BSA reference), also seen less robustly in HUVEC transwells; NOT a brain BBB model
intact_cargo_recovery: Authors report majority of basal FVIIa intact by TCA/SDS-PAGE, but basal-lane data not shown; independently shown intact recycled protein in supernatant does not establish basolateral transport of APC
quantitative_results: Caveolin-1 colocalization r~0.945 in HUVEC; Rab11 sorting 10-30 min; CHO-EPCR transwell ~4-fold FVIIa vs BSA; 3-um pore membrane and Evans Blue-BSA control
safety_mechanism: Ligand competition with protein C/APC, potential FVIIa kinetics and systemic clearance; receptor recycling not sufficient to infer safe noncompetitive short-peptide shuttle
strengths: Independent surface binding and receptor-positive controls; multiple trafficking probes; APICAL/BASAL measurement, gross leak marker, biochemical intactness statement
limitations: Major data in EPCR-overexpressing CHO; HUVEC non-BBB endothelium; 3um pores, no reported TEER or BBB-specific tight junction validation; basal intactness data not shown; in-vivo extravascular staining was bone/joint (not brain); APC apical-to-basal transport not directly quantified
figures_tables: PDF pp. 4-12: Figs 1-8; crucial Fig 6 (recycling) and Fig 8A (FVIIa transwell)
evidence_grade: Direct receptor-dependent cell-model trafficking and FVIIa transwell transport; indirect for native BBB delivery

short_title: APC triggers human brain endothelial EPCR/PAR1 calcium signaling
species_models: Early-passage primary human brain microvascular endothelial cells from autopsy and HUVEC
molecule_format: Native full-length activated protein C protease; zymogen protein C; inactive Ser360Ala APC; blocking versus nonblocking antibodies
main_endpoint: Rapid intracellular Ca2+ signalling through EPCR-dependent PAR1 activation in primary human BEC
receptor_specificity: RCR252 EPCR ligand-site antibody abrogates APC Ca2+ signal while nonblocking EPCR antibody RCR92 does not; PAR1 cleavage-site antibodies block; PAR2/PAR3 controls ineffective
luminal_access: Human cultured primary brain EC display functional EPCR binding; does not establish polarized native luminal epitope accessibility in stroke
internalization_trafficking: None measured; signaling rather than uptake/trafficking study
quantitative_results: APC Ca2+ EC50 0.23 +/- 0.02 nM; mean maximal increment reported 278.3 +/- 19.5 nM; n=70 measurements (NOT 70 human donors)
safety_mechanism: Strong evidence that blocking natural APC-EPCR engagement perturbs PAR1/Ca2+ signaling; RCR92 proves epitope-dependent blocking can be avoided for Ca2+ readout, NOT universal safety
strengths: Human brain microvascular endothelial cells, protease-inactive and zymogen controls, site-specific mAbs, PAR specificity, thapsigargin ER-store control
limitations: Cultured autopsy BEC; 1-minute APC stimulation and calcium readout, not chronic signalling/coagulation/BBB integrity; no transcytosis, peptide cargo, or human in-vivo luminal mapping
figures_tables: PDF pp. 2-4: Fig 1 (dose-response/controls), Fig 2 (PAR1 and EPCR blocking), Fig 3 (ER Ca2+)
evidence_grade: Direct human brain EC receptor-specific signaling; no transport endpoint

short_title: TM4SF1 extracellular EL2 epitope and human-vessel targeting
species_models: Human HUVEC, ECFC, HDF/HEK293 transfectants; mouse MS1 cells; human ECFC/MSC Matrigel vessels in nude mice
molecule_format: Human TM4SF1, human/mouse TM4SF1 chimeras, glycan-deficient N129/159G mutant; anti-human 8G4 monoclonal IgG1 (not a peptide)
main_endpoint: Epitope mapping, live-cell surface binding, human-vessel targeting and vascular destruction by naked antibody
receptor_specificity: 15 antibodies isolated; 13 bind live human surface; EL2 swaps restore 8G4 staining in mouse-human chimera; neither 8G4 nor other 12 EL2 antibodies recognize native mouse TM4SF1; isotype controls
luminal_access: Strong binding to cultured human endothelial surface; in-vivo human vascular network, NOT native human brain or mouse-stroke BBB luminal quantification
internalization_trafficking: Surface 8G4 binding; internalized vesicle patterns illustrated; directional intracellular itinerary examined in 2015 paper
directional_bbb_delivery: NO; no polarized brain EC transwell, no blood-to-brain transport in any model
intact_cargo_recovery: NOT TESTED; vessel depletion and FITC-dextran vascular volume ≠ functional peptide shuttle
quantitative_results: EL2 is 48 amino acids; human/mouse EL2 ~73% identity (versus original compiled full extracellular identity 77.27%); two N-glycosylation motifs at human N129/N159 vs mouse second N142; 8G4 Kd ~1 nM; 8G4 vessel model ~52.7-fold reduction in human CD31, ~9.3-fold reduction in vascular volume
safety_mechanism: Naked 8G4 in implanted human-vessel model destroyed growing vessels, while in vitro HUVEC migration/tube assays reportedly unchanged at 100 ug/mL (data not shown): do not assume innocuous binding; potential Fc/vascular-context mechanisms
strengths: Species swap, glycan perturbation and live-cell staining support epitope specificity; in-vivo vascular model proves targetability
limitations: Not BBB; perfused human Matrigel neo-vessels not CNS endothelium; distinct human/mouse glycans; no peptide/transcytosis readout; some key null findings data not shown
figures_tables: Fig 1A-F (PDF p4); Fig 3 (p8); Fig 4 (p9); text pp5,7-9
evidence_grade: Direct human peripheral endothelial accessibility + molecular species/glycan validation; no BBB transport

short_title: TM4SF1-bound 8G4 internalizes to cytoplasm and nucleus
species_models: HUVEC, human gastric tumor vessel micrographs; comparator E-selectin binding; some human tumor cell lines
molecule_format: Human surface glycoprotein TM4SF1 and full monoclonal 8G4 antibody (not short peptide)
main_endpoint: Cellular internalization, trafficking and subcellular distribution, not BBB passage
receptor_specificity: 8G4 vs isotype mouse IgG1; dynasore versus pitstop-2/chlorpromazine/bafilomycin inhibitors; E-selectin uptake comparator
luminal_access: Immuno-nanogold luminal surface staining in human gastric cancer tumor vessels stronger than abluminal; native human brain microvessel not assessed
internalization_trafficking: 8G4-TM4SF1 uncoated vesicles, dynamin sensitive / clathrin inhibitor insensitive; microtubule association; cytoplasmic and nuclear/nuclear-pore localization
directional_bbb_delivery: NO; nuclear-associated uptake and delivery are intracellular, not abluminal BBB transcytosis
intact_cargo_recovery: Whole 8G4 antibody staining observed intracellularly, not intact abluminal cargo; molecular integrity of exported peptide not tested
quantitative_results: Surface signal loss ~20.8%, 52.2%, 95% at 2,4,24h; after 4h at 37C surface staining 37.8 +/-6.5% vs dynasore 90.1 +/-1.7%; pitstop-2 39.1 +/-3.2%
safety_mechanism: Efficient uptake can enable toxin exposure in vessels and peripheral tissues; no direct direct toxicity assay for short peptide in this paper
strengths: Nanogold EM plus confocal Z-stacks and inhibitor comparisons with isotype and E-selectin controls
limitations: 4h/24h signal loss may include shedding; nuclear passage mechanism speculative; pharmacologic inhibitor specificity limited; no brain EC barrier/polarity assay, no intact-peptide export
figures_tables: Figures 1-4 (PDF pp16-19); Supplementary figures S1-S4 pp20-25
evidence_grade: Direct TM4SF1 antibody uptake and intracellular tracking in peripheral human endothelium; no BBB transport

short_title: TM4SF1-enriched microdomains recruit intracellular signaling machinery
species_models: Human HUVEC, B16F10 tumors and cutaneous ear wounds in surviving Tm4sf1 +/- versus wildtype mice
molecule_format: Endogenous TM4SF1 microdomain signaling complexes; h8G4 co-IP; shRNA depletion; no engineered brain shuttle cargo
main_endpoint: TM4SF1-associated intracellular trafficking and physiologic consequences of lowering TM4SF1 expression
receptor_specificity: Isotype hIgG1 co-IP control; reverse IP (PLCgamma1, HDAC6, alpha-tubulin); clathrin-negative control; shRNA controls; wildtype littermates
luminal_access: TMED cell surface on cultured HUVEC and activated endothelium; no native brain-stroke luminal quantification
internalization_trafficking: 12/18 screened signaling proteins associate with surface TMED, ten remain associated at 2h; PI4K and PKCalpha transient; PLCgamma1/HDAC6 co-IP; cytoskeletal/nuclear-directed intracellular routing, NOT extracellular shuttling
directional_bbb_delivery: NO; no polarized BBB, brain parenchymal tracer or apical-basal transport assay
intact_cargo_recovery: NO external intact therapeutic cargo; endogenous signaling association is not transported synthetic peptide
quantitative_results: WT vs +/- tumor volume day12 ~1855 +/-475.6 vs 297 +/-51.9 mm3; day21 WT vs +/- ear wound closure 60.83 +/-4.42% vs 12.09 +/-2.57%; KD >90% mRNA; reported 12/18 recruited, 10 persistent at 2h
safety_mechanism: Impaired wound healing, reduced vascular proliferation and altered microtubule acetylation with TM4SF1 lowering; authors cite embryonic hemorrhage/null lethality from OTHER study (not novel experimental endpoint here)
strengths: IP/reverse IP and gene perturbation plus in vivo littermate comparisons; exposes essential vascular biology
limitations: Co-IP/presence is not direct cargo co-transport or transcytosis; HUVEC and tumor/wound models not ischemic BBB; full supplementary mechanistic details not supplied; knockout phenotypes cannot be equated to ligand-binding peptide toxicity
evidence_grade: Direct endothelial signaling and vascular-function evidence; no BBB transport

short_title: TM4SF1-directed ADC vascular homing and toxicity
species_models: Mouse MS1 EC and HEK293±mTM4SF1; C57BL/6 safety mice; nude mouse VEGF-A-induced ear neovessels
molecule_format: Mouse-reactive 2A7A and Fc-effector-attenuated 3m2A7A (L234A/L235A/G237A) antibodies; mc-3377 cytotoxic payload LP2; isotype-matched ADC control; NOT short peptide
main_endpoint: Blood-facing targeting of VEGF-induced peripheral neovessels and selective antibody-drug mediated vessel damage and systemic survival
receptor_specificity: TM4SF1 transfected vs untransfected HEK293; isotype ADC/naked antibodies; paired mock virus ear; effector-attenuated vs parent antibody
luminal_access: 3m2A7A antibody colocalizes with VEGF-induced new vessel luminal surface by immuno-EM at 6h; no brain EC or ischemic BBB test
internalization_trafficking: Target-associated vascular cytotoxic effects compatible with intracellular payload delivery; in this study no direct polarized brain transcytosis
directional_bbb_delivery: NO; newly formed peripheral vessel targeting/destruction not BBB delivery
intact_cargo_recovery: NO intact peptide/cargo crossing; Evans blue albumin accumulation reflects plasma content/vessel changes, not transcytosis
quantitative_results: 3m2A7A homing 19 +/-2.7 vs 4.3 +/-1.5 nanogold per 300nm luminal surface (~4.42x); ADC cell EC50 ~2-4 nM; after q4d×4 at 5mg/kg survival parent 65% vs 3m 100%; at 10mg/kg 5% vs 35% (control ADC 100%); 3mg/kg single dose disrupted angiogenic vessels within 48h; repeated 3mg/kg q2d×3 caused local necrosis
safety_mechanism: High-dose ADC-associated mortality and local new-vessel necrosis; Fc-effector attenuation improves tolerance but does not eliminate payload toxicity; naked antibody did not produce comparable cytotoxicity in their tested setting
strengths: Orthogonal luminal EM, model tissue control, isotype ADC, untransfected cells and survival dose comparison
limitations: Tumor-surrogate ear model, cytotoxic mc-3377 payload, antibody not peptide; no transport through brain BBB; cannot extrapolate ADC lethality to non-toxic shuttle without payload; Figures caption has linker conjugation ambiguity (lysine vs cysteine) to clarify if relevant
figures_tables: Figs 1-5 (PDF pp3-7); discussion p8; supplement is referenced but not included
evidence_grade: Direct peripheral luminal targeting and ADC-associated vascular-toxicity evidence; no BBB transport

short_title: ECSCR potentiates KDR signaling and angioblast migration
species_models: Zebrafish embryos and ECSCR morphants; human HUVEC and HPAEC endothelial cultures
molecule_format: Endogenous ecscr/ECSCR; ECSCR morpholino knockdown with human mRNA rescue; ECSCR siRNA; V5-tagged ECSCR overexpression; VEGF165; VEGFR2/KDR and FLT1, NOT dosed shuttle or peptide ligand
main_endpoint: Angioblast positioning and endothelial migration, VEGF-KDR phosphorylation, proliferation and annexin apoptosis signal
receptor_specificity: Two separate zebrafish ecscr morpholinos; human ECSCR mRNA rescue; control morpholino and lacZ siRNA; FLT1 selectivity; VEGFR inhibitor phenocopy (not direct receptor binding control)
luminal_access: Overexpressed ECSCR localized to actin-rich HUVEC protrusions; not tested native luminal human brain endothelium; membrane expression ≠ blood-facing epitope validation
internalization_trafficking: Punctate spatial colocalization with KDR near protrusive cell edge; NO demonstrated selective ligand-induced ECSCR uptake or ECSCR-directed cargo trafficking
directional_bbb_delivery: NOT DEMONSTRATED; no polarized BBB transport, brain perfusion or parenchymal cargo measurement
quantitative_results: ECSCR siRNA ~70% transcript decrease; serum-stimulated HUVEC migration 38% of lacZ control and HPAEC 57%; VEGF migration 117% vs 157% of unstimulated; annexin-positive apoptosis ~11% vs ~36%; VEGF-stimulated [3H]thymidine ~104% vs ~281% of unstimulated; Table 1 MO2 10ng normal 22% vs control MO 83%, human mRNA rescue normal 62%; KDR pTyr951/996/1059/1175 and PLCβ3 pSer537/1105 decreased; FLT1 phosphotyrosine unaffected
safety_mechanism: Silencing modifies VEGF-responsive migration, proliferation and apoptosis; could interfere with vascular remodeling or stroke healing if peptide blocks signaling; genetic loss-of-function ≠ nonblocking peptide safety
strengths: Two MO modalities, human mRNA rescue, multiple human primary EC types, receptor phosphorylation specificity, functional assays; Fig 4 and Table 1 include quantitative readouts
limitations: Developmental zebrafish and peripheral cultured ECs, not human stroke brain EC; receptor gain/loss not exogenous binder; no receptor-specific internalization/transport; a morpholino dose has toxicity and cell behavior endpoints vary by context
figures_tables: Figs 1-6, Table 1 (PDF pp3-7); relevant control and rescue Table 1 p4; additional supplement referenced but not uploaded
evidence_grade: Strong mechanistic signalling and vascular migration; surface evidence in culture only; NONE for shuttle transcytosis

short_title: ECSCR associates with VEGFR2 and controls its intracellular proteolysis
species_models: Human HUVEC, porcine aortic EC/KDR overexpression, HEK293 and mouse bEND.3 endothelial cells; zebrafish kdrl:GFP morphants; human placenta and hemangioma sections
molecule_format: Endogenous/tagged ECSCR and KDR/FLT1; human ECSCR ΔC, EMCN chimera and TMswap; VEGF165/VEGF121; SU5416, bafilomycin A1, chloroquine; genetic/biochemical complexes NOT externally administered ECSCR binding shuttle
main_endpoint: ECSCR-KDR physical association, ligand-dependent perinuclear/endosomal co-localization, VEGFR2 activation/degradation and endothelial phenotype
receptor_specificity: Endogenous anti-ECSCR co-IP vs control serum, FLT1 negative, EMCN and receptor domain swaps, reciprocal IP, two siRNAs; VEGF121 vs VEGF165, SU5416 and pH blockers
luminal_access: Cell surface ECSCR and KDR context supported in HUVEC; tissue staining for placental/muscle and peripheral human vessels; native brain luminal presentation NOT tested
internalization_trafficking: After VEGF165, ECSCR-KDR-NRP1 co-localization in perinuclear vesicle-like structures ~10 min; partial HRS/ESCRT-0, adjacent to RAB7, not RAB11; ECSCR knockdown attenuates KDR proteolysis; NOT an ECSCR peptide/cargo transport assay
directional_bbb_delivery: NOT DEMONSTRATED: trafficking of KDR inside EC is not trans-endothelial transport or basolateral release
intact_cargo_recovery: NOT TESTED; no ECSCR-targeted intact ligand/peptide recovery
quantitative_results: ECSCR/KDR co-IP peaks at ~10 min VEGF165, basal by ~30 min; VEGF121 weak co-IP despite receptor activation; ECSCR overexpression raised surface KDR ~30%, total KDR ~40%; combined subeffective kdrl 1.4ng + ecscr 6.4ng morpholinos caused delayed ISV sprouting in 66/75 embryos (88%) vs kdrl alone 2/12 (16.7%), ecscr alone 1/25 (4%) and kdrl+control 1/12 (8.3%)
safety_mechanism: ECSCR controls KDR availability, downstream Akt/ERK and receptor degradation; blocking/agonistic epitope might alter VEGF neurovascular repair; native role is context-dependent; increased ECSCR protein in placenta/trophoblast, hemangioma and major peripheral vessels raises peripheral sink concerns
strengths: Endogenous receptor co-IP, specificity vs FLT1 and EMCN, epitope-independent TM swaps, pharmacological modulation, quantified zebra genetic interaction, human tissue staining
limitations: Some domain/soluble-ECD tests data not shown; co-IP cannot establish direct contact; no receptor-selective extracellular ligand; co-localization is NOT cargo flux; no native ischemic BBB, stroke brain, or intact drug delivery; supplementary Figs/Tables referenced not supplied
figures_tables: Figs 1-7 and Table 1 (PDF pp4-8); Figs 3-5 trafficking; Fig 7 non-endothelial trophoblast expression
evidence_grade: Strong ECSCR-KDR signaling/trafficking evidence; no shuttle uptake; no BBB transport

short_title: ECSCR loss and gain alter systemic endothelial insulin and angiogenesis biology
species_models: Mice: Ecscr knockout WT comparator, endothelial TIE2-Ecscr transgenic, genetically restored ECSCR, eNOS deficient double genotype, chow and high-fat diet; aortic EC, muscle capillaries, WAT, BAT and peripheral tissues
molecule_format: Genetic modulation of ECSCR/ARIA; endogenous insulin, endothelial PTEN/PI3K-Akt/eNOS, L-NAME; radiolabeled 125I-insulin uptake into skeletal muscle; no exogenous ECSCR-binding peptide
main_endpoint: Systemic insulin availability, skeletal muscle perfusion, glucose tolerance, adipose neovascularization, thermogenesis, metabolic safety
receptor_specificity: Knockout, endothelial Tie2 overexpression, endothelial genetic rescue, eNOS gene dependency and L-NAME pharmacologic dependency; wild type/chow/HFD controls; receptor-mediated binding/uptake absent
luminal_access: Ecscr high in WAT/BAT and endothelial stromal vascular fraction, but NOT directly demonstrated on native brain luminal membranes
internalization_trafficking: Insulin delivery to muscle supported by higher perfusion and 125I-insulin-associated tissue levels after Ecscr loss; ECSCR itself not shown to bind, internalize, or transcytose insulin or a peptide
directional_bbb_delivery: NO BBB test; insulin passage/availability in skeletal muscle cannot be assigned to ECSCR as a transcytotic shuttle and may reflect eNOS-mediated perfusion
intact_cargo_recovery: NO intact engineered cargo across brain endothelium; 125I-insulin counts in muscle do not by themselves establish molecular intactness or ECSCR-dependent transcytosis
quantitative_results: Loss of Ecscr enhanced insulin-stimulated EC pAkt/p-eNOS, muscle perfusion and 125I-insulin tissue signal (Fig 2); improvement lost on L-NAME/eNOS deletion (Fig 3); Ecscr KO increased insulin sensitivity and resisted high-fat obesity, hepatic steatosis, WAT/BAT hypoxia (Figs 1,4-6); Tie2-Ecscr overexpression caused converse phenotypes (Figs 3,7), and endothelial rescue reversed knockout improvements (Fig 8); study reports group n and significance in legends, not one transferable effect size
safety_mechanism: Functional ECSCR manipulation profoundly affects peripheral insulin signaling, nitric-oxide vascular physiology, adipose angiogenesis and metabolism; not evidence that a passive nonblocking binder is toxic; endpoint-specific monitoring required
strengths: Loss, gain and endothelial rescue combined with pharmacologic/genetic eNOS tests and physiological outcomes; two diets and multiple peripheral tissues
limitations: Mouse chronic genetic manipulations, nonbrain vascular beds, not acute poststroke peptide exposure; 125I-insulin accumulation may contain perfusion/clearance contributions; no ECSCR–insulin physical binding, no polarized BBB transport or peptide toxicity
figures_tables: Figs 1-8 (PDF pp3-10); substantial supplement referenced but not uploaded; primary molecule insulin/eNOS is NOT ECSCR cargo
evidence_grade: Strong systemic physiological/safety and off-organ evidence; not BBB shuttle evidence
